question: Within one documented BRFSS release, how do reported cost barriers to care differ across income groups?
initial_approach: Start with the questionnaire and coverage notes; reproduce one prevalence table, then estimate weighted group differences and uncertainty using the documented survey design.
official_source: CDC BRFSS 2024 data, questionnaire, codebook and sampling documentation
access_and_feasibility: Public files listed; confirm retained variables, wording, missingness and reporting areas. The page notes public-file modifications and incomplete state coverage. No data downloaded or audited.
skills_and_compute: Survey interpretation; complex-survey statistics and R or equivalent for analysis; ordinary CPU and memory after checking file size.
contribution_to_test: A justified descriptive comparison or measurement check beyond the closest existing work.
likely_output_forms: Substantive research blog; preprint or journal article if the developed contribution warrants it
example_paper_title: A systematic review of publications assessing reliability and validity of the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS), 2004-2011
example_paper_authors: Carol Pierannunzi; Shaohua Sean Hu; Lina Balluz
reference_verification: Title, authors, year and DOI checked against PubMed PMID 23522349 and publisher; Crossref request rate limited.
evidence_qualification: Methods example reviews measurement evidence for earlier BRFSS instruments; it does not validate the selected current variables. Self-reported access differences are not causal effects or clinical findings.

question: How do primary-care scheduling simulation papers published in 2020-2025 represent missed appointments and differences in access?
initial_approach: Make a small literature comparison; define eligible service models and code their assumptions, access measures and validation evidence. Develop an evidence map if the fuller search is feasible.
official_source: PubMed search and PubMed Central open-access article records
access_and_feasibility: Public search and some full texts; record unavailable texts and coverage limits. An open-access-only sample must be labeled. No comprehensive search or screening completed.
skills_and_compute: Reading, source extraction and domain review; spreadsheet sufficient for a first task; review-methods help for a full synthesis.
contribution_to_test: A useful map of model assumptions and evidence that extends or updates the nearest reviews.
likely_output_forms: Substantive research blog; review preprint or journal article
example_paper_title: An analysis of the academic literature on simulation and modelling in health care
example_paper_authors: S C Brailsford; P R Harper; B Patel; M Pitt
reference_verification: Title, authors, year and DOI checked against Crossref and publisher abstract; publisher full-text access restricted.
evidence_qualification: Published example classifies healthcare-modeling literature; it is not evidence that this narrower question is new. Nonreporting of an access measure does not establish absence from a model or harm in practice.

question: At fixed capacity, how do first-come-first-served and shortest-expected-task dispatch affect tail waiting times when a repair-service queue receives bursty demand?
initial_approach: Build a small discrete-event model with documented synthetic arrivals and task classes; check a simple analytical case, then compare both rules across the same conditions and report waiting times by task class.
official_source: SimPy resource documentation and explicitly specified synthetic experiment inputs
access_and_feasibility: Public documentation; synthetic inputs need no service records. State which task-duration information is available when dispatch occurs. Service data would be needed for a real-site claim.
skills_and_compute: Queueing, simulation design and basic programming; small CPU runs, repeated random seeds and a bounded runtime pilot.
contribution_to_test: A reproducible explanation of conditions and tradeoffs, including whether a rule harms long tasks.
likely_output_forms: Full conference paper; suitable preprint; substantive research blog
example_paper_title: Strengthening the reporting of empirical simulation studies: Introducing the STRESS guidelines
example_paper_authors: Thomas Monks; Christine S. M. Currie; Bhakti Stephan Onggo; Stewart Robinson; Martin Kunc; Simon J. E. Taylor
reference_verification: Title, authors and DOI checked against Crossref and publisher PDF; online 2018 and issue 2019 dates distinguished.
evidence_qualification: Reporting methods example, not a validated repair-service model. Synthetic results are conditional on arrivals, task information, service distributions and dispatch rules.

question: How sensitive are simple resource-constrained project scheduling rules to duration uncertainty on a small, fixed subset of PSPLIB instances?
initial_approach: Reproduce deterministic schedules for selected small instances; verify precedence and resource feasibility. Apply stated duration scenarios and compare fixed dispatch rules using repeated runs and matched budgets.
official_source: Technical University of Munich PSPLIB benchmark library
access_and_feasibility: Public generated benchmark sets and reference solutions; choose and identify a bounded subset. Duration distributions would be hypothetical extensions, not measured PSPLIB project uncertainty.
skills_and_compute: Engineering management; optimization and simulation; basic scheduling code, ordinary CPU and a runtime pilot.
contribution_to_test: A justified robustness comparison or replication with a clearly documented extension.
likely_output_forms: Full conference paper; suitable preprint; journal article if supported; substantive research blog
example_paper_title: PSPLIB - A project scheduling problem library
reference_verification: Title, authors, year and DOI checked against Crossref; official PSPLIB site confirms the benchmark purpose but lists an earlier citation year.
evidence_qualification: The example establishes a benchmark approach, not a new scheduling question. Generated instances and assumed uncertainty do not establish performance on real projects.

question: For one documented contrast in public mouse mammary-cell RNA-seq data, how sensitive are gene rankings and effect estimates to defensible filtering and normalization choices?
initial_approach: Inspect GEO metadata and processed counts; reproduce a supported analysis baseline. Compare prespecified analysis choices while retaining the biological replicate structure and reporting uncertainty.
official_source: NCBI GEO GSE60450 series metadata and processed gene-count supplementary files
access_and_feasibility: Public processed counts listed; no raw-read alignment needed for the proposed first stage. Confirm sample mapping, count type, pairing and the intended contrast before analysis.
skills_and_compute: Bioinformatics and count-data statistics; R/Bioconductor or equivalent; CPU and RAM estimated from processed files.
contribution_to_test: A transparent replication or sensitivity result that is useful beyond a tutorial.
likely_output_forms: Substantive research blog; methods preprint; journal or full conference paper if the contribution develops
example_paper_title: Moderated estimation of fold change and dispersion for RNA-seq data with DESeq2
example_paper_authors: Michael I Love; Wolfgang Huber; Simon Anders
reference_verification: Title, authors, year and DOI checked against Crossref and PubMed/publisher; GEO record inspected separately.
evidence_qualification: A methods paper for count-data analysis, not proof that every choice is valid for this dataset. Small biological samples limit inference; a changing gene shortlist does not establish a biological mechanism.

question: For one NIST Lennard-Jones reference state, how do timestep choices affect pressure estimates and energy stability under an otherwise matched molecular model?
initial_approach: First match the stated potential, cutoff, ensemble, density and units. Reproduce one reference condition, then vary timestep while checking equilibration, numerical error, correlated samples and uncertainty.
official_source: NIST Lennard-Jones fluid reference results and official LAMMPS documentation
access_and_feasibility: Public reference results and conditions; source files and software suitability still need checking. Begin with a small system and runtime pilot; GPU access is not assumed.
skills_and_compute: Computational Natural Sciences: molecular simulation and numerical methods; small CPU pilot, with later resources justified by required precision.
contribution_to_test: A reproducible numerical-sensitivity study or implementation comparison with a stated scientific use.
likely_output_forms: Substantive research blog; arXiv preprint where in scope; computational-methods journal article
example_paper_title: LAMMPS - a flexible simulation tool for particle-based materials modeling at the atomic, meso, and continuum scales
example_paper_authors: Aidan P. Thompson et al.; last author Steven J. Plimpton
reference_verification: Title, author list, year and DOI checked against Crossref, publisher and official LAMMPS citation documentation.
evidence_qualification: Software methods example. Agreement with NIST checks the specified calculation; it does not validate a real material or make the numerical-sensitivity question novel.

question: Within one Consumer Expenditure Survey year, how do household energy-spending shares differ across income groups, and how sensitive are the comparisons to measurement choices?
initial_approach: Start by reproducing a relevant official table; use documented spending categories, income definitions, survey weights and variance methods. Compare justified definitions of spending share and income grouping.
official_source: US Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Expenditure Survey public-use microdata and getting-started documentation
access_and_feasibility: Public Interview and Diary files listed separately. Confirm which source measures the chosen spending, imputation and time unit; repeated interviews must not be treated as independent households.
skills_and_compute: Survey economics and statistics; statistical software and ordinary CPU; a first contribution can check the published tables and documentation.
contribution_to_test: A clear measurement or distributional finding beyond existing tables.
likely_output_forms: Substantive research blog; suitable preprint; journal article if the developed contribution warrants it
example_paper_authors: Bruce D. Meyer; Wallace K. C. Mok; James X. Sullivan
reference_verification: Title, authors, year and DOI checked against Crossref and American Economic Association publisher record.
evidence_qualification: Methods/context example explains survey error; it is not an energy-expenditure analysis recipe. Survey error and income definitions affect comparisons; descriptive differences do not identify price or policy effects.

question: Under the same hypothetical cash-transfer budget, how do flat and income-targeted transfers change a defined poverty gap in one public CPS ASEC sample?
initial_approach: Reproduce the chosen baseline poverty measure using its documented income and family units. Specify two hypothetical transfer rules, calculate static outcomes, and vary take-up and the targeting threshold.
official_source: US Census Bureau CPS Annual Social and Economic Supplement public data and documentation
access_and_feasibility: Public annual files listed; select a release and verify weights, poverty units, thresholds and income period. This first model does not require restricted EU-SILC or a full tax-benefit model.
skills_and_compute: Distributional economics, microsimulation and survey statistics; ordinary CPU after a small pilot.
contribution_to_test: A transparent account of distributional tradeoffs and assumption sensitivity.
likely_output_forms: Substantive research blog; suitable preprint; economics or policy journal article if supported
example_paper_title: EUROMOD: The European Union tax-benefit microsimulation model
reference_verification: Title, authors and DOI checked against Crossref and journal; publisher dates the issue 2013 while Crossref published field says 2012. Publisher year retained.
evidence_qualification: Transferable static-microsimulation example, not a CPS implementation. Hypothetical arithmetic scenarios exclude behavioral and general-equilibrium responses unless modeled; they are not predictions of an actual policy.

question: How much do age differences in self-reported political interest change with official weights and alternative missing-response treatment in the ANES 2020 cross-sectional sample?
initial_approach: Use the official questionnaire and codebook to define one pre-election interest measure; compare weighted descriptive estimates with an explicitly labeled unweighted diagnostic and justified missing-response scenarios.
official_source: American National Election Studies 2020 public release, questionnaire and codebook
access_and_feasibility: Public CSV and documentation links listed. Confirm release corrections, fresh-cross-section membership, valid responses, age grouping and matching pre-election weights before analysis.
skills_and_compute: Survey interpretation and design-based statistics; ordinary CPU; a reading contribution can map questionnaire wording and coding first.
contribution_to_test: A useful replication or measurement-sensitivity explanation, not a claim that weighting itself is new.
likely_output_forms: Substantive research blog; suitable preprint; journal replication or methods article if supported
example_paper_title: Struggles with Survey Weighting and Regression Modeling
reference_verification: Title, author, year and DOI checked against the author-hosted published article; DOI resolves to the Statistical Science publisher record.
evidence_qualification: Methods example discusses survey weighting and modeling, not this ANES result. An unweighted diagnostic is not a population estimate; a cross-sectional age association is not an effect of aging.

question: How sensitive are segregation outcomes in a simple Schelling-style model to sequential versus simultaneous updates at fixed preference and vacancy settings?
initial_approach: Begin with the documented browser model; specify both update procedures, including vacancy conflicts. Match initial conditions, repeat random runs, and compare prespecified spatial outcomes and time to stopping.
official_source: Northwestern University NetLogo Segregation model and documentation
access_and_feasibility: Public model and browser demonstration; page states CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 for this model. Check license compatibility before copying or redistributing code. Modified rules require explicit implementation checks.
skills_and_compute: Agent-based modeling and spatial-measure interpretation; browser for learning; small CPU experiments for a study.
contribution_to_test: A documented replication and update-rule sensitivity result with clear limits.
likely_output_forms: Substantive research blog; suitable arXiv preprint; full conference or journal methods paper if supported
reference_verification: Title, author, year and DOI checked against Crossref and publisher; publisher adds a footnote marker to the title.
evidence_qualification: Original model paper demonstrates an abstract mechanism; the NetLogo implementation is a later adaptation. Model patterns do not establish real residents' preferences or explain observed segregation by themselves.

question: In a fixed sample of one agency's Data.gov records, how consistently are reuse terms and update frequency documented?
initial_approach: Define the agency, sampling rule and snapshot date. Code a small sample manually against published field definitions; document ambiguous records and expand only if the comparison is useful.
official_source: Data.gov catalog API documentation and DCAT-US v1.1 field definitions
access_and_feasibility: Public documentation and metadata access route checked; live API retrieval and field mapping still need a pilot. Data.gov metadata are not the underlying datasets; optional and conditional fields must be distinguished.
skills_and_compute: Policy implementation, source coding and metadata interpretation; spreadsheet for a first contribution; optional small script, ordinary CPU.
contribution_to_test: A bounded transparency or implementation finding with an explicit sampling frame.
likely_output_forms: Substantive research blog or technical essay; policy/informatics journal article if supported
example_paper_title: Open data policies, their implementation and impact: A framework for comparison
reference_verification: Title, authors, year and DOI checked against Crossref and publisher abstract; author-deposited manuscript identified separately.
evidence_qualification: Comparative policy framework example, not a Data.gov compliance test. Missing optional metadata do not establish legal noncompliance, lack of dataset updates, unusability, or policy impact.

question: Can the documented did package minimum-wage example be reproduced, and how do group-time and conventional two-way fixed-effect summaries differ on the same example sample?
initial_approach: Reproduce the package baseline on mpdta; state the target comparison, aggregation, treatment timing and uncertainty. Compare like quantities where possible and explain differences rather than treating estimators as interchangeable.
official_source: CRAN did package reference manual and author-supplied mpdta example dataset
access_and_feasibility: Public manual documents mpdta as 500 counties in 2003-2007, a subset of the paper dataset. Confirm package/data version and reuse terms; this is not the full study or a current policy sample.
skills_and_compute: Causal inference and panel-data statistics; R or equivalent, ordinary CPU; methods review needed for causal interpretation.
contribution_to_test: A reproducibility account or justified methods comparison, explicitly a replication rather than a new policy-effect estimate.
likely_output_forms: Substantive research blog; suitable preprint; replication/methods journal article if supported
example_paper_authors: Brantly Callaway; Pedro H. C. Sant'Anna
reference_verification: Title, authors, year and DOI checked against publisher and official package documentation; Crossref request rate limited.
evidence_qualification: Methods paper and supplied example demonstrate staggered-adoption estimation. Parallel-trends, anticipation, overlap and dependence assumptions still matter; successful reproduction does not independently establish a policy effect.
